result.title: RSIgen: Reciprocal Self-Improvement for Agentic Visual Generation
result.summary: Agentic visual generation produces experience that can improve the native understanding (agent) and generation roles of a unified multimodal backbone, but task success alone does not determine which role should learn. Generator updates can also make the agent's action supervision stale. We introduce RSIgen, a task-centric reciprocal self-improvement framework linking learning allocation, supervision refresh, and recursive curriculum construction. Dynamic Responsibility Routing (DRR) uses matched interventions on evidence, inputs, and supported actions to select learning recipients and construct compatible training targets. After generator learning, RSIgen re-evaluates the relative utility of tested actions with branch inputs held fixed to refresh agent supervision; the retained roles then construct the next curriculum. Across BAGEL, Qwen-Image, and Wan-Image-7B, RSIgen improves AgentGen-Bench Full Overall9 by 3.2--3.3 points over a three-cycle SearchGen adaptation with action costs. Wan controls support allocation gains at matched role-level training exposure, refresh gains at a matched adaptation budget, and benefits from updated curriculum sources while recipients continue learning. In blind evaluation on 200 real-user requests, pooled tie-adjusted preference scores against the same baseline reach 70.0% for task completion and 64.9% for visual quality.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RSIgen，一个任务中心的互惠自改进框架：用匹配干预的 Dynamic Responsibility Routing 决定统一多模态骨干中理解（agent）与生成两种角色谁该学习，并在生成器更新后固定分支输入重评动作效用以刷新 agent 监督，再据此递归构建课程。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「责任分配 + 监督刷新」线索可能与 LVR 中轨迹训练的贡献分配、更新后陈旧监督问题相关，可供核查；但论文面向 agentic 视觉生成而非 VLM 推理，迁移到 latent 推理状态是否成立尚需核实。
